headline: October: cocoa alternatives go to market, Barry Callebaut bets on fermentation, FDA opens salt substitutes
summary: Cocoa was the month's story: Galy launched cultured cocoa in the US, Planet A Foods moved into cocoa powder replacement, and Barry Callebaut launched its Flavourcode fermentation platform, together the biggest set of partner and competitor moves for Belcolade.
Sugar and egg reduction advanced through start-up partnerships, notably Oobli with Cosun on a chocolate sugar replacer and MOA Foodtech with Espiga I+D on bakery egg replacement.
US bakers are pushing fibre and protein (Grupo Bimbo, Calise, Rudi's), and Roquette and Palsgaard launched gluten-free and cake texture ingredients that compete with Puratos mixes and improvers.
Easing cocoa prices and Lindt's price cuts suggest chocolate pricing pressure ahead, so the case for cocoa-saving products needs revisiting as costs fall.

Regulatory: the FDA salt-substitute rule for standardized breads (effective 14 December 2026), a federal synthetic-dye ban bill, California sugar warnings and the push for a federal ultra-processed food definition all point to reformulation demand.
